answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using physical distance-bounding challenges. To register, each agent must promptly return an echo to synchronized probes, proving its network proximity under speed-of-light limits across physical copper and fiber links. This forces an attacker to deploy scarce, geographically dispersed hardware and dedicated transit per identity. However, routing jitter creates a ripple of false rejections that unfairly penalizes agents on congested connections.
